$comment: REAL frames captured from a live OpenClaw gateway. Not written by hand.
Captured 2026-08-03 from openclaw 2026.7.1-2 (0790d9f) running in the
SairiOS VM guest, started with:
openclaw gateway --dev --auth none --allow-unconfigured --port 18789
No provider credential was involved. The handshake, the request/response
cycle and the method/event vocabulary are all reachable without one, which
is why this much could be verified before anyone supplies a key.
Values that vary per connection (nonce, connId, timestamps, durations) are
kept as captured rather than normalised, so the shapes stay honest. Tests
assert on structure, not on these values.

envelope.$comment: Three frame kinds. This is the part our placeholder got wrong: it switched on `type` expecting an event NAME there, but `type` is the category and `event` carries the name.

$comment: client.id and client.mode are CLOSED ENUMS, enforced server-side.
The gateway rejects anything else with INVALID_REQUEST naming the exact
path, which is how these were found:
invalid connect params: at /client/id: must be equal to one of the
allowed values; at /client/mode: must be equal to one of the allowed
values
ids   (GATEWAY_CLIENT_IDS):   webchat-ui, openclaw-control-ui,
openclaw-tui, webchat, cli, gateway-client, openclaw-macos,
openclaw-ios, openclaw-android, node-host, test, fingerprint,
openclaw-probe
modes (GATEWAY_CLIENT_MODES): webchat, cli, ui, backend, node, probe, test
NOTE: the protocol.md shipped with this very package shows
`"mode": "operator"` in its connect example. That value is not in the
enum and the gateway refuses it. `operator` is a ROLE, not a mode.
SairiOS connects as gateway-client/backend: the documented trusted
same-process path for a loopback control-plane client, which may omit
`device` rather than going through pairing.

rejection.$comment: What a bad connect actually returns. Worth keeping: it is the shape our error path has to read.

error.message: invalid connect params: at /client/id: must be equal to one of the allowed values; at /client/mode: must be equal to one of the allowed values

$comment: The gateway advertised 218 methods and 30 events. These are the ones a
SairiOS turn would use. Recorded so the mapping is reviewable before it
is implemented, rather than discovered one 500 at a time.
Our placeholder invented `session.prompt`, `session.created`,
`message.delta`, `tool.call`, `ui.specification`, `session.done`. None of
those exist.
`exec.approval.requested` is the interesting one: OpenClaw has its own
approval round trip, and SairiOS already has a permission broker with the
same shape. Those two must be wired to each other rather than allowed to
both prompt, or a user answers the same question twice.

responses.$comment: Real payloads, truncated where long. `models.list` is empty because no provider is configured — that emptiness is exactly the shape of the remaining gap.
